root_cause.text: The ath12k driver incorrectly applied WoW (Wake-on-Wireless) offload operations to all links in a multi-link connection, but the WCN7850 firmware only supports WoW on the primary link, causing a firmware crash.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "firmware crashes due to WoW offloads enabled on both primary and secondary links" and the patch adds `if (arvif != &arvif->ahvif->deflink) continue;` in multiple WoW-related functions (ath12k_wow_cleanup, ath12k_wow_set_wakeups, ath12k_wow_nlo_cleanup, ath12k_wow_arp_ns_offload, ath12k_gtk_rekey_offload) to skip secondary links, ensuring offloads are configured only on the primary (deflink) link.

intent_record.intent_summary: In ath12k_wow_cleanup, skip non-default link entries to prevent duplicate WoW cleanup per virtual interface.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check inside the list_for_each_entry loop to skip arvif entries that are not the default link (deflink) of their parent ahvif.
intent_record.how: Previously, ath12k_wow_vif_cleanup was called for every arvif in the list. Now only the default link arvif for each virtual interface is processed, preventing redundant cleanup calls.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard against configuring WoW wakeups on non-default vdev links, ensuring only the default link is set up.
intent_record.what: Added a condition to skip arvifs that are not the default link (deflink) of their ahvif in the loop that sets WoW wakeups.
intent_record.how: The loop now only processes arvifs that are the default link, skipping all others, which prevents configuring WoW wakeups on non-default links.

intent_record.intent_summary: In ath12k_wow_nlo_cleanup, only process the default link vif to avoid incorrectly cleaning up NLO for non-default links.
intent_record.what: Added an if condition inside the list_for_each_entry loop that checks if the current arvif is the default link (deflink) of its ahvif; if not, the loop continues to skip it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the loop now only processes arvifs that are the default link of their ahvif, skipping non-default links, thereby restricting the subsequent cleanup operations to default link vifs only.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip ARP/NS offload configuration for virtual interfaces that are not the default link, ensuring offload is only applied on the primary link.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check inside the loop over list of arvifs that compares each arvif to the deflink member of its associated ahvif; if they are not equal, the loop continues to the next iteration.
intent_record.how: This ensures that ARP/NS offload configuration (enable/disable) is only applied when the virtual interface is the default link, skipping non-default links to prevent unintended offload settings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to prevent GTK rekey offload on non-default links, ensuring configuration is only applied to the default link (deflink).
intent_record.what: Added a condition inside the list_for_each_entry loop to skip arvif entries that are not the default link (deflink) of their parent vif.
intent_record.how: The new guard causes the function to only process the default link of each virtual interface, preventing GTK rekey offload from being configured on non-default links.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add guards to ensure that cleanup and configuration operations (WoW, NLO, GTK rekey) are only applied to the default link in multi-link scenarios.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by adding guards to restrict WoW, NLO, and GTK rekey operations to the default link, preventing the firmware crash caused by applying these operations to non-primary links in multi-link connections.
The group's intent directly addresses the root cause by guarding against WoW configuration on non-default vdev links, ensuring only the primary link is set up, which prevents firmware crashes.

The group's changes explicitly skip ARP/NS offload for non-default links, ensuring offload is only applied on the primary link. This directly addresses the root cause where WoW offload was incorrectly applied to all links, leading to firmware crash on WCN7850.

candidates.rationale: This statement applies WoW cleanup to every virtual interface (arvif) in the list without checking whether it is the primary link. On a multi-link connection, this causes cleanup on non-primary links, which the firmware does not support, leading to a crash.

This statement sets WoW wakeups on every virtual interface, including non-primary links. The firmware only supports WoW on the primary link, so configuring wakeups on secondary links causes a firmware crash.

The loop iterates over all virtual interfaces (links) without discrimination, leading to subsequent operations being applied to all links. This structural lack of a guard for the primary link is part of the root cause.
Same as above: The loop structure in ath12k_wow_set_wakeups causes the operation to be applied to all links, including non-primary, contributing to the vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement calls ath12k_wow_vif_set_wakeups on every virtual interface in the loop, including non-primary links. The firmware only supports WoW wakeup configuration on the primary link, so applying it to secondary links causes a firmware crash.

This statement calls ath12k_wow_vif_cleanup on every virtual interface in the loop, including non-primary links. Performing WoW cleanup on secondary links is unsupported by the firmware and leads to a crash.

This loop iterates over all virtual interfaces (links) in ath12k_wow_set_wakeups without checking if the link is the primary (default) link, causing the subsequent WoW wakeup configuration to be applied to all links instead of only the primary.

This loop iterates over all virtual interfaces (links) in ath12k_wow_cleanup without checking if the link is the primary (default) link, causing WoW cleanup to be applied to all links instead of only the primary.

bic_trace_step.reason: In ath12k_wow_cleanup() and ath12k_wow_set_wakeups(), the code iterates over all arvifs in ar->arvifs list (via list_for_each_entry) and applies WoW operations to every vif. For example, ath12k_wow_set_wakeups() iterates over 'list_for_each_entry(arvif, &ar->arvifs, list)' and calls ath12k_vif_wow_set_wakeups(arvif, wowlan). Similarly, ath12k_wow_cleanup() iterates all arvifs. However, the WCN7850 firmware only supports WoW on the primary link; applying WoW to secondary links causes a firmware crash. The code does not check whether the vif belongs to the primary link, nor does it skip non-primary vifs. Therefore, the vulnerable construct is present and no fix is included.
